one_line: Sultan of Delhi (1351–1388 CE), builder of canals and monuments yet a stern, often brutal ruler.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium height, sturdy build with the bearing of a seasoned ruler.
appearance.face: Oval face, wheatish North Indian complexion, deep-set sharp brown eyes with dark circles, straight prominent nose, neatly trimmed medium-length beard and moustache with a few grey streaks, slightly furrowed brow, default expression calm but intense and authoritative.
appearance.hair: Dark brown hair, straight and kept short under a tall cylindrical quilted turban (dastār) in muted deep green with a narrow gold band at the base and a simple white cloth tail wrapped around and tucked at the back; no feathers or fantastical ornaments.
appearance.costume: Long-sleeved quilted cotton tunic (char-taqiyā coat) reaching mid-calf in deep rust-red, visibly padded in a subtle vertical quilting, worn over a light beige linen kurta seen at the collar and cuffs; dark olive-green narrow churidar-style trousers; a wide plain leather belt in dark brown with a simple bronze buckle at the waist; over the shoulders a soft woollen shawl in dull grey with a thin dark-red border, usually draped over the left shoulder; simple dark brown leather boots reaching just above the ankle; minimal jewellery—small plain gold hoop in one ear and a modest signet ring on the right hand.
appearance.signature: A straight-backed Indo-Persian sword (talwar) with a slightly curved single-edged steel blade, iron hilt with a disc pommel and cross-guard, carried sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings, worn suspended from his right hip on the belt.

ref_desc: Firuz Shah Tughlaq is a late-middle-aged, wheatish-complexioned Sultan with deep-set intense eyes, short hair under a tall deep-green turban, rust-red quilted tunic, olive churidar, grey shawl, dark boots, and a sheathed dark-brown-belted talwar, in earthy reds, greens and browns.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Firuz Shah Tughlaq: a late-middle-aged, sturdy North Indian Sultan with an oval wheatish face, deep-set sharp brown eyes, straight nose, and a medium-length neatly trimmed beard with a few grey streaks, his expression calm but intense and authoritative. His short dark brown hair is mostly hidden beneath a tall cylindrical quilted turban in muted deep green with a narrow gold band at the base and a simple white cloth tail wrapped around and tucked at the back. Dress him in a long-sleeved, mid-calf quilted cotton tunic in deep rust-red with visible vertical padding, worn over a light beige linen kurta visible at the collar and cuffs, and dark olive-green narrow churidar-style trousers. Add a wide plain dark-brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle at his waist, and dark brown ankle-high leather boots. Drape a soft woollen shawl in dull grey with a thin dark-red border over his left shoulder, hanging across his back and chest. Show minimal jewellery: a small plain gold hoop in one ear and a modest signet ring on his right hand. At his right hip, show his signature Indo-Persian talwar, slightly curved, sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings, suspended from the belt. Use a grounded palette of rust red, deep green, dark olive, beige, dark brown and grey, and present him front-facing, three-quarter, and back views to clearly show face, hair, costume details, and sword placement.
